generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table, never NULL; never overwritten by duplicate-share or boundary rules.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the parent table's generated key pool, excluding a reserved subset of parent keys that is deliberately left unreferenced so at least one parent row per parent table has no children; allow NULL only where the column is nullable; never NULL in NOT NULL FK columns.
generic_sampling_rules.text_generic: Short title-case words from a small vocabulary; allow near-variants (case changes, one-character edits, leading/trailing spaces) for boundary columns; allow NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Sample uniformly from the explicit enum list; boundary values listed in per_column_exceptions are merged into the enum pool and may fall outside the enum domain (documented as a deliberate boundary variant); allow NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_range: Uniform integer within the stated range; include boundary values and one step outside where the atomic summary lists a boundary.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For each nullable column, generate at least one NULL row per instance and set the NULL share to the compact database share (5-30% for Albums.Title; 0.10 for all other nullable columns).
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct: For columns flagged with duplicates_for_distinct, repeat values so that distinct count is 20-50% of row count; never apply to a primary-key or UNIQUE-tuple column.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_values: About 10% of text values are fresh (not in the literal pool) to avoid overfitting.
generic_sampling_rules.table_size: Generate exactly the specified table_sizes_per_instance rows per table (no jitter, no +/-20% band, no exponential growth); parent tables are filled before children.

generation_specification.uncertainty: Original tables are empty, so no formulas could be verified against shown rows; all rules are inferred from the atomic-operation summary and schema constraints. Enum domains for Albums.Type, Vocals.Type, Instruments.Instrument and Performance.StagePosition are inferred from the literal pool and may be incomplete; boundary variants (e.g. '%Studio', 'o', 'sared', 'drms') are deliberately outside the semantic enum domain and are merged into the enum pool. Songs.SongId comparison_boundary with string literals is non-applicable to an integer PK and is not generated. The null_in_count_column pattern is a query-shape pattern with no value effect. Duplicate-share rules are applied only to columns not in a PK UNIQUE tuple; the atomic summary's duplicate_share targets for Songs.Title and Instruments.Instrument are honored, while Vocals.SongId, Vocals.Type, Instruments.BandmateId and Band.Id are excluded by the applicability flag.

issues.title: Primary-key duplicates; generated rows not deduplicated against existing compact rows
issues.evidence: Construction execution feedback reports pk_duplicates=21 and 13/20 instances rejected as 'new_integrity_failures' (only 7 valid). Band appended 302 skipped rows of 353 attempted, Instruments 518 skipped, Vocals 407 skipped. The most likely cause is single-column integer PKs that collide: instance.py assigns sequential PKs from _pk_start(schema,t)=max(compact)+1, but then sample_fresh_primary_keys() dedups only generated rows against reserved compact tuples; the deduped length is not used to shrink child counts and (crucially) the writer inserts row-by-row and the skipped rows indicate real PK/UNIQUE collisions. Also the integer PK is drawn from two paths: samplers may produce a range sampler for SongId/AId/Id (spec.ranges has ('Songs','SongId')->(1,None) etc.), but then build_random_instance overwrites with sequential start+i — so the PK is fine; the collisions are instead that _apply_duplicate_share() rewrites flagged columns AFTER the PK uniqueness step, and Band.Id / Instruments.BandmateId are themselves in spec.dup, so dup redistribution reintroduces duplicate PK / duplicate unique-key values, and those rows are then rejected by SQLite (increasing rows_skipped for Band and Vocals).
issues.requested_revision: Apply _apply_duplicate_share only to non-PK, non-unique columns (drop Band.Id, Instruments.BandmateId, Vocals.SongId if they form part of a PK/UNIQUE); alternatively dedup after dup-share and drop offending rows before writing so the writer never has to skip PK rows. Ensure generated PK and UNIQUE tuples never collide with compact rows or each other so pk_duplicates=0 and rows_skipped=0 for PK tables. Re-run and confirm validity=20/20, pk_duplicates=0.

issues.title: Songs.Title null-rate above compact share and NULL-rule interaction with dup_share
issues.evidence: Songs.Title: NULL 53/523 (~10%) — within stated target, but _apply_null_rule is applied before _apply_duplicate_share, and Songs.Title is in spec.dup, so dup-share may overwrite planted NULLs (the code skips None when reassigning, so NULLs survive — acceptable). More problematic: Band.Firstname NULL 9/114 (~8%) and Band.Lastname 16/114 (~14%) — these exceed nullable-columns reported shares only if Firstname/Lastname are truely nullable; the schema does not mark them NOT NULL, so this is allowed. No blocking defect here beyond confirming the NULL share matches spec.
issues.requested_revision: No change strictly required; verify Firstname/Lastname target shares (0.10) are met and that spec.null_targets includes them (it does).

issues.title: Enum domains inferred, not guaranteed complete (uncertainty noted in spec)
issues.evidence: The specification explicitly says 'Enum values for Albums.Type, Vocals.Type, Instruments.Instrument and Performance.StagePosition are inferred from the literal pool and may be incomplete.' Semantic formulas for these columns are thus not evidence-backed; only the atomic summary's comparison_boundary values (e.g. vocals.type 'shared','lead','drums','sared') are corroborated. The boundary pools in spec.py (_DEFAULT_BOUNDARY) match the atomic summary values, which is good.
issues.requested_revision: Keep as-is but document enums as uncertain; do not treat them as hard semantic constraints. This is not blocking because the program only samples from them and does not enforce with SQL.

issues.title: Table sizes per instance were overridden by choose_table_sizes relative to the specification
issues.evidence: Specification gives exact table_sizes_per_instance (Songs 40, Albums 20, ...), and load_specification copies these into spec.sizes. But build_random_instance calls choose_table_sizes(schema, rng, spec) which samples sizes 0.5x–1.5x (or a growing 1..30*4^lvl capped 2500) and IGNORES the exact spec sizes. Execution shows a single instance produced Songs=523+compact rows and Tracklists=1441+compact rows, far exceeding specified sizes of 40/60. This contradicts per_table_sizes in the specification.
issues.requested_revision: Make table sizes respect the specification: sample around the specified size (e.g. within a small band, or exactly the specified size with modest jitter), rather than the unrelated 0.5x–1.5x / exponential-growth rule. Document the intended variation band in the specification to stay consistent.

issues.title: Songs.SongId 'null_in_count_column' has no implementable semantics
issues.evidence: The atomic pattern null_in_count_column with example 'added SELECT(COUNT(songs.songid)) removed SELECT(COUNT(*))' is about how COUNT is applied in queries (COUNT(col) vs COUNT(*)), not a property of generated SongId values. The specification targets count_column='Songs.SongId' but the program has no effect for this (correctly). The example even shows fallback 'JOIN(instruments.songid=songs.songid),TABLE(songs)' as alternate. This is not a generation rule.
issues.requested_revision: Note as a non-generative pattern; no program change required. Optionally remove the per_column_exceptions entry to avoid implying the program should act on it.

issues.title: Nullable FK Vocabulary tracking: Vocals.Bandmate generated NULL share reported as absent
issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback does not list Vocals.Bandmate, though schema makes it nullable FK and spec.null_targets includes it, and Vocals rows were generated (762 rows) with Bandmate from the FK path. The NULL rule requires at least one planted NULL and a compact share; the program fills FK NULLs via fill_foreign_keys_consistently with spec.null_share (0.05 for Vocals.Bandmate via _DEFAULT_NULL_SHARE / spec). But the NULL was not observed in the report. This should be verified.
issues.requested_revision: Verify Vocals.Bandmate generates NULL rows with share ~0.05 and at least one NULL per instance. If it does not appear, ensure fill_foreign_keys_consistently honors null_share for nullable FK children and that spec.null_share has a (Vocals, Bandmate) entry (it does via _DEFAULT_NULL_SHARE). Confirm post-fix the nullable report shows Vocals.Bandmate.

issues.title: Comparison-boundary planted literals may be overwritten by generic samplers / not guaranteed to appear
issues.evidence: Songs.SongId boundary targets values ['Flash','flash'] (equal_and_one_step_from Songs.Title). But Songs.SongId is an INTEGER PK overwritten by sequential keys, so the value 'Flash' can never be generated — and shouldn't be for an integer PK. This is a designer-side inconsistency (a TEXT literal routed to an integer column). Supported pairs separated 77/99 is high, so the core boundary literals (TEXT columns) are evidently planted for Songs.Title, Vocals.Type, Instruments.Instrument, Band.Lastname/Firstname, Albums.Type, matching the _DEFAULT_BOUNDARY pools.
issues.requested_revision: Designer should drop Songs.SongId from comparison_boundary with string values (or reinterpret as a Songs.Title boundary); it cannot be honored on an integer PK. Engineer code already handles it gracefully by ignoring non-applicable boundary on PKs.

unresolved_checks: The exact mechanism producing the 21 pk_duplicates and 13 invalid instances was inferred (dup-share on PK/unique columns and/or dedup ordering); confirm root cause after the fix.
Vocals.Bandmate NULL generation not observed in feedback; verify.
Whether choose_table_sizes behavior is intended variation or a spec/program mismatch — recommend aligning to specified sizes.
reviews.summary: The program runs reproducibly and implements the boundary literal pools, enum domains, FK dependencies, and NOT NULL handling. However, it fails integrity on 13/20 instances with pk_duplicates=21, and it ignores the specified table_sizes_per_instance (generating hundreds of rows where tens were specified). Both are blocking and require revision (engineer: fix PK/UNIQUE dedup ordering + dup_share on PK columns, enforce spec sizes; designer: drop the misplaced Songs.SongId string boundary and clarify table-size variation).

issues.evidence: tscore_gen/instance.py choose_table_sizes() applies a +/-20% jitter to every table size: `lo = max(1, int(round(base * 0.8))); hi = max(lo, int(round(base * 1.2))); sizes[t] = rng.randint(lo, hi)`. The specification's generic_sampling_rules.table_size explicitly states: 'Generate exactly the specified table_sizes_per_instance rows per table (no exponential growth, no 0.5x-1.5x jitter)'. Execution feedback confirms the violation: rows_added per 20 instances are Songs 806 (spec 40 -> 40.3 avg, within band but not exact), Albums 390 (spec 20 -> 19.5), Band 308 (spec 15 -> 15.4), Instruments 1225 (spec 60 -> 61.25), Performance 973 (spec 50 -> 48.65), Tracklists 1196 (spec 60 -> 59.8), Vocals 775 (spec 40 -> 38.75). These deviate from the exact per-instance sizes and are only consistent with jittered sizes.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the +/-20% jitter in choose_table_sizes() and use the exact spec.sizes value for each table (fallback only when a table is absent from the spec). Re-run generation and confirm rows_added equals table_sizes_per_instance * n_instances for every table.

issues.evidence: The specification's generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk states 'leave some parent keys unreferenced so parent rows without children exist', and the atomic summary lists unmatched_join_rows for many FK columns (e.g. Songs.SongId parent_rows_without_children, Band.Id parent_rows_without_children). In instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently() draws FK values uniformly with replacement from the full parent pool (`rng.choice(pv)`), so with 40-60 child rows over 15-40 parent keys, unreferenced parents are not guaranteed and are not deliberately constructed. The construction_pairs feedback shows 79/99 pairs separated, but there is no evidence that parent-rows-without-children is systematically produced; the spec's unmatched_join_rows targets are not implemented by construction.
issues.requested_revision: Add explicit construction of unreferenced parent keys: after filling FK columns, ensure at least one parent key per parent table is not referenced by generated child rows (e.g. reserve a subset of parent keys and exclude them from the FK draw), while still respecting the NULL share. Document this in the spec's dependencies and verify with a join-count check.

issues.evidence: The specification's supporting_evidence states 'The original tables are empty, so no formulas could be verified against shown rows; all rules are derived from the atomic-operation summary and schema constraints.' The atomic summary lists comparison_boundary for Songs.SongId with string literals ('Flash', 'flash') and equal_and_one_step_from Songs.Title; the spec correctly drops these as non-applicable to an integer PK. However, the spec also lists null_targets including 'Vocals.Bandmate' and 'Tracklists.SongId' as nullable, but the schema declares Vocals.Bandmate and Tracklists.SongId as FK columns without NOT NULL — consistent. The spec's semantic_rules_and_formulas for Albums.Type lists enum values ('Studio','Live','Compilation','EP','Single') but the atomic summary's comparison_boundary targets for Albums.Type include '%Studio', 'o', 'O', 'STUDIO' which are not in the enum; the spec's boundary pool includes them but the enum formula does not, so generated Albums.Type values from the enum sampler will never produce '%Studio' or 'o' unless the boundary pool is merged. In instance.py the enum branch merges boundary values only when `key in spec.boundary`, which is true for Albums.Type, so this is handled — but the spec's semantic formula and boundary pool are inconsistent in intent and should be reconciled.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile Albums.Type: either extend the enum formula to include the boundary variants or explicitly document that boundary variants are sampled outside the enum domain. Also document that the empty original tables mean all rules are inferred, and flag which rules (e.g. enum domains for Albums.Type, Vocals.Type, Instruments.Instrument, Performance.StagePosition) are uncertain and may be incomplete.

issues.evidence: The specification's generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct states 'repeat values so that distinct count is 20-50% of row count; never apply to a primary-key or UNIQUE-tuple column.' In instance.py _apply_duplicate_share() skips columns in PK/UNIQUE tuples via _dup_eligible(), which correctly excludes Band.Id (PK), Instruments.BandmateId (part of Instruments UNIQUE tuple), Vocals.SongId (part of Vocals UNIQUE tuple), and Vocals.Type (part of Vocals UNIQUE tuple). However, the spec's _DEFAULT_DUP includes ('Band','Id') and ('Instruments','BandmateId') and ('Vocals','SongId') and ('Vocals','Type'), and the spec's supporting_evidence explicitly says these are 'dropped because ... would break uniqueness'. The spec's per_column_exceptions still lists duplicates_for_distinct for Vocals.SongId and Vocals.Type and Instruments.Instrument without noting the PK/UNIQUE exclusion, so the spec and program disagree on which columns receive the duplicate share. Execution feedback does not show distinct-count evidence per column, so this is unresolved.
issues.requested_revision: Update the spec's per_column_exceptions to mark duplicates_for_distinct as inapplicable for columns participating in PK/UNIQUE tuples (Vocals.SongId, Vocals.Type, Instruments.BandmateId, Band.Id), matching the program's _dup_eligible() behavior. Add execution evidence of distinct-count shares for the eligible columns (Songs.Title, Instruments.Instrument).

issues.evidence: The specification's generic_sampling_rules.null_share states 'For each nullable column, generate at least one NULL row and set the NULL share to the compact database share (5-30% for Albums.Title; small share elsewhere).' Execution feedback shows NULL counts for nullable columns but omits Vocals.Bandmate (listed in null_targets) and Tracklists.SongId is shown (242/1196 = 20.2%, above the 'small share' 5% target and above the spec's 0.10 default). Vocals.Bandmate is absent from the nullable_columns feedback entirely, so it is unresolved whether NULLs were planted there. Also Albums.Title NULL 69/390 = 17.7% (within 5-30%), but Tracklists.SongId at 20.2% exceeds the spec's 0.10 default and the 'small share' guidance.
issues.requested_revision: Verify and report NULL counts for Vocals.Bandmate; align Tracklists.SongId's null share with the spec's stated small share (0.10) rather than the observed 20.2%, or update the spec to state the intended share. Ensure every nullable column in null_targets has at least one NULL row per instance.

issues.evidence: The specification's semantic_rules_and_formulas include 'Vocals.Type IS NULL OR Type IN (lead, shared, backing, drums)' and 'Instruments.Instrument IN (drums, guitar, bass, keyboard, vocals, violin)'. The atomic summary's comparison_boundary targets for Vocals.Type include 'sared', 'SARED' (misspellings) and for Instruments.Instrument include 'drms', 'DRMS', 'dru', 'DRU' — these are outside the enum domains. The spec's boundary pools include them, and instance.py merges boundary values into the enum sampler when `key in spec.boundary`, so generated values can violate the stated enum formula. This is a spec/program inconsistency: the semantic formula claims a closed enum but the boundary pool injects out-of-domain values.
issues.requested_revision: Either relax the semantic formula to 'Type IN (...) OR Type IN (boundary variants)' or remove the misspelled boundary variants from the boundary pool. Document the intended interaction between enum domains and comparison_boundary variants.

unresolved_checks: Whether Vocals.Bandmate received planted NULLs (absent from nullable_columns feedback).
Whether parent-rows-without-children is systematically produced for all FK parents (no join-count evidence provided).
Whether distinct-count shares for duplicates_for_distinct columns fall in 20-50% (no per-column distinct evidence provided).
Whether the 79/99 separated construction pairs cover all atomic-summary patterns or only a subset; the feedback does not break down separation by pattern group.

issues.evidence: Atomic summary lists Songs.SongId comparison_boundary with string literals ('Flash') and a self-referential predicate 'songs.songid = songs.title = 'Flash''; the specification correctly drops these as non-applicable to an integer PK (supporting_evidence.Songs.SongId). Vocals.SongId comparison_boundary 'equal_and_one_step_from Songs.SongId' is also not implemented as a value rule (only FK draw from parent pool).
issues.requested_revision: No change required for pass; optionally document explicitly that Vocals.SongId 'equal_and_one_step_from' is satisfied structurally by FK sampling from Songs.SongId rather than by a dedicated boundary sampler.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows Vocals.Bandmate is a nullable column in the spec (null_targets, null_share 0.10) but the nullable_columns report lists no 'Vocals.Bandmate: generated rows: NULL ...' line, and rows_added Vocals=776 vs 40*20=800 suggests ~24 rows dropped by _dedup_keys after NULL planting (NULL Bandmate tuples collide on UNIQUE(SongId,Bandmate)). The NULL rule is still satisfied per instance (at least one NULL, non-NULL present) but the reported share may be below 0.10 after dedup.
issues.requested_revision: No blocking change; optionally re-plant NULLs after final dedup or report Vocals.Bandmate NULL counts so the 0.10 share is verifiable. Per instruction 7 this does not block a pass.

issues.evidence: Performance rows_added=943 vs 50*20=1000 and Tracklists=1194 vs 60*20=1200: rows are dropped by _dedup_keys on UNIQUE(SongId,Bandmate) / UNIQUE(AlbumId,Position) after FK sampling, so per-instance table sizes fall short of the exact spec sizes (table_size rule says 'exactly the specified rows').
issues.requested_revision: No blocking change; optionally retry FK draws on UNIQUE-tuple collision to hit exact sizes. Current behavior is documented in instance.py step 7 and does not violate integrity.

issues.evidence: Enum domains for Albums.Type, Vocals.Type, Instruments.Instrument, Performance.StagePosition are inferred from the literal pool (uncertainty field). Boundary variants like '%Studio', 'o', 'sared', 'drms' are deliberately out-of-domain and merged into the enum pool; this is documented and consistent with the atomic summary's comparison_boundary targets.
issues.requested_revision: No change; the uncertainty is acknowledged and the merged-pool behavior is intentional.

Exact per-instance table sizes not achieved for Performance/Tracklists/Vocals due to UNIQUE-tuple dedup; integrity preserved (0 violations, 0 skipped rows).
reviews.summary: Program ran cleanly (20/20 valid, 0 FK/NOT NULL/PK violations, 0 skipped rows, reproducible). Specification implements exact sizes, NULL shares, boundary pools, enum domains, duplicate-share exclusions for PK/UNIQUE-tuple columns, and reserved-parent-key logic for unmatched_join_rows. Construction feedback: 79/99 eligible pairs separated, 0 unknown executions. Semantic rules are supported by the atomic summary; uncertain enum domains are documented. Minor size shortfalls and unreported Vocals.Bandmate NULL share are noted but do not block a pass.
